message.content:
Here’s a quick rundown of the **federal Canadian holidays that create “official” long‑weekends in 2023** (i.e., holidays that fall on a Friday or a Monday, or are observed on a Monday when they land on a weekend).  

| Holiday | Date in 2023 | Notes |
|---------|--------------|-------|
| **New Year’s Day** | **Mon Jan 02** (observed) | New Year’s Day fell on Sunday Jan 01, so the holiday was observed on Monday Jan 02. |
| **Good Friday** | Fri Apr 07 | Good Friday itself is a statutory holiday, giving a three‑day weekend. |
| **Victoria Day** | Mon May 22 | Celebrated on the last Monday before Canada Day; gives a long weekend. |
| **Canada Day** | **Mon Jul 03** (observed) | Canada Day fell on Saturday Jul 01, so the holiday was observed on Monday Jul 03. |
| **Labour Day** | Mon Sep 04 | Labour Day is always on the first Monday in September. |
| **Thanksgiving** | Mon Oct 09 | Thanksgiving is always on the second Monday in October. |

> **Quick note:**  
> *Family Day* (the third Monday in February) is a statutory holiday in several provinces (Ontario, British Columbia, Alberta, Saskatchewan, Manitoba, New Brunswick, Prince Edward Island, and Nova Scotia). In 2023 it fell on **Mon Feb 20** in those provinces, creating a long weekend there.  
> *Remembrance Day* (Thu Nov 11) is a statutory holiday in most provinces, but because it fell on a Thursday in 2023 it did **not** create a long weekend (unless a province chooses to observe it on Monday).

If you’re building an app, you can pull this data programmatically with the `holidays` Python package:

```python
import holidays

canada_holidays = holidays.Canada(years=2023)
for date, name in sorted(canada_holidays.items()):
    print(date, name)
```

This will give you all federal holidays (and their observed dates) for 2023, which you can then filter for those that fall on a Friday or Monday to identify long weekends.
